a_note: Read calls and transcripts, trigger actions from your own scripts.
act_note: Sign-ins, sign-outs and password changes on your own account.
backup_section_note: Where archives are written, and what goes in them.
empty_body: A fresh installation starts with defaults only. Phone lines, the phones on them and the numbers callers dial are all set up on the Numbers and phones screen.
empty_title: Nothing configured in this section yet
err_body_after: . The container is running as a user without write permission on that volume. Your changes are still in this form and will be applied once the permission is fixed.
ev_key_sign_in_succeeded: Signed in with an SSH key
f_announce_help: Callers are told at the start that the call is recorded. Austria requires both parties to be aware, so turning this off is a decision.
f_backup_path_help: A mounted network share or a USB disk. Leave empty and no backup is taken at all.
f_backup_recordings_help: Roughly 60× larger archives. Leaving this off means restores have transcripts but no audio to prove what was said.
f_calendar_help: The agent proposes and books only inside the hours you expose here.
f_daily_help: One message each evening with the day’s calls.
f_hostname_help: What this machine calls itself on your network.
f_instname_help: Shown in the browser tab and in notification emails.
f_keep_tr_help: Transcripts stay searchable after the audio is gone.
f_lang_help_general: The default across the whole installation: screens, assistant replies, emails, exports and notifications. German, English and Arabic are fully translated.
f_lang_help_profile: Applies to everything you see and everything sent in your name — screens, emails, exports and notifications.
f_llm_base_url_help: Leave it empty for the default. Point it at a gateway, or at a model on your own machine, to use those instead.
f_llm_key_help: Stored encrypted and never shown again. A model on your own machine usually accepts any value.
f_llm_model_help: The name the endpoint expects, for example gpt-4o-mini.
f_llm_provider_help: The kind of endpoint. Leave it empty to run without a model: the agent still takes messages, and says plainly that nobody is answering yet.
f_ports_help: Web interface, SIP signalling and the RTP media range.
f_proxy_help: Trust X-Forwarded headers from your proxy only.
f_public_url_help: Used in links inside notification emails and in the app pairing code.
f_record_help: Callers are told at the start of every call.
f_redact_help: Removes digit sequences that look like payment cards.
f_send_as_help: Shown as the sender on every notification.
f_sms_gw_help: Timed out four times this week.
f_smtp_port_help: 587 with STARTTLS works almost everywhere; 465 is implicit TLS.
f_smtp_ssl_help: Encrypted from the first byte. Used by port 465. Leave off unless your provider says otherwise.
f_smtp_tls_help: Upgrade a plain connection to an encrypted one. On for port 587, which is the usual case.
f_tls_help: Let’s Encrypt renews automatically; a self-signed certificate makes phones complain.
f_tool_failed_help: The most useful alert — this is how you learn an SMS never arrived.
f_tz_help: Used for opening hours, timestamps and retention.
host_note: Where this installation answers on your network.
inv_admin_note: Everything, including settings, backups and team members.
inv_err_email: That does not look like an email address.
inv_expires: The link works once and expires in seven days. Resending makes a new link and kills this one.
inv_mailed: A copy also went by email.
inv_not_mailed: No mail server is configured — copy the link and send it to them yourself.
inv_note: They choose their own username and password when they open the link. The link works once and expires in seven days.
inv_reception_note: Answer calls, read transcripts, edit contacts and the calendar.
inv_viewer_note: See calls and transcripts. Cannot change anything.
live_failed: These settings could not be loaded.
live_note: These settings are stored in the database and take effect without a restart.
live_secret_kept: The password was left as it was — retype it to change it.
m_inward_note: Point an MCP client at this address and it can run the business phone: read transcripts, change an assistant, add a routing rule, place a call. This is how you drive Tel-Agent from a model or from your own agent instead of from this interface.
m_outward_note: The tool servers your assistants reach during a call, their tools and their health, live on their own page.
m_warning: Anything you switch on here can be done by whatever holds the key, without a person confirming it. Write is off by default for that reason — a client that can add a routing rule can also silence your line.
mail_test_failed: The mail server refused or did not answer. The log carries its exact words.
mail_test_no_email: Your account has no email address, so there is nowhere to send the test.
mail_test_not_configured: No mail server is configured. Fill in the host and sender above, save, then test.
model_test_not_configured: No model is connected yet. Fill in the provider, the model and the key above, then save.
model_test_unreachable: Nothing answered at that address. Check the endpoint, and that this machine can reach it.
offline_body_after: . A wrong password here is the usual cause.
offline_body_before: The provider rejected the last three attempts with
offline_title: SIP registration failed — check the credentials below
p_changed_done: Password changed. Every other signed-in browser and phone was signed out.
p_devices_note: Every browser and phone signed in to this account, except the one you are using now.
p_signout_done: Signed out everywhere else. This session stays.
pw_hint: A sentence you can remember beats a short one you cannot.
pw_locked: Too many attempts. Try again shortly.
pw_mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
pw_reused: This is one of your recent passwords. Choose a different one.
pw_too_short: That password is too short. A sentence you can remember beats a short one you cannot.
pw_wrong_current: That is not the current password.
role_reception_note: Takes calls, edits contacts and the calendar.
role_viewer_note: Reads calls. Changes nothing, answers nothing.
sec_advanced_body: Everything here can break call handling. Nothing on this tab needs to be touched for a normal installation.
sec_api_body: How your own software talks to Tel-Agent, and how Tel-Agent talks back. Everything here is on your network — there is no Tel-Agent cloud in the middle.
sec_channels_body: Where customers reach you. Web chat is built; the rest arrive at Milestone 3.
sec_general_body: Name, language and time zone for this installation. These defaults apply everywhere unless a screen overrides them.
sec_integrations_body: The calendar and the gateways the agent uses during a call.
sec_mcp_body: Tel-Agent exposes its own tools so something else — a model, a script, your own agent — can drive this installation.
sec_notifications_body: Where Tel-Agent tells you something needs a human. Failures always reach you, even if everything else is switched off.
sec_profile_body: Your own account on this installation. Changing these affects you only, not the business settings.
sec_recording_body: How long audio and transcripts are kept. Austrian businesses usually keep recordings for 90 days and transcripts for a year.
sec_users_body: Who can sign in to this installation. Everyone here can read every transcript, so keep the list short.
smtp_note: Tel-Agent has no mail server of its own — it sends through yours.
title: Settings
tool_get_assistant_desc: Read an assistant’s instructions, voice, sources and tools.
tool_list_calls_desc: Search calls and read transcripts, filtered by date, number or outcome.
tool_place_call_desc: Ring a number and have an assistant handle the conversation.
tool_set_routing_rule_desc: Add, edit or remove a rule that decides who answers.
tool_system_health_desc: Service status, disk, answer latency — the same data as the health page.
tool_update_assistant_desc: Change instructions, greeting or which sources an assistant may read.
u_roles_note: Taking a call also needs a phone registered to that person — the role alone is not enough.
u_workspace_note: A role applies to this workspace only. The same person can be Admin here and Reception somewhere else, and each workspace has its own numbers, contacts and call history.
w_note: Sent as JSON, signed, retried three times.
w_replay_note: Failed deliveries are kept for a day and can be replayed from the log.
wc_captcha_help: reCAPTCHA v3 scores visitors without asking them to identify a bicycle. It is Google's, and it sees your visitors — leave it off if that is not acceptable to you. The rate limit applies either way.
wc_enabled: Show the chat on those sites
wc_error_no_key: This installation has no encryption key, so a secret cannot be stored.
wc_error_no_origins: Add the address of the site that will show the chat before switching it on.
wc_error_origin: One of those is not an address. Write it as https://example.com, with no path.
wc_note: A chat bubble on your own site. No account with anybody, no review, nobody's approval.
wc_origins_help: One address per line, like https://example.com — scheme and domain only, no path. This is what stops another site from embedding your chat, so nothing works until at least one is here.
wc_secret_help: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again after you save it.
wc_secret_keep: Leave blank to keep the saved one
wc_snippet_help: Just before </body>, on every page that should show the chat.
wc_threshold_help: 0.5 is Google's default. Higher refuses more bots and more real customers.
